Households in Nuevo Laredo will pay more for electricity starting today, Sunday, November 1, as the federal summer subsidy comes to an end, according to El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo.

The summer subsidy scheme applied from April through the end of October, and from November 1 the regular domestic tariff returns, according to the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) as reported by Noreste Digital on October 30. The change does not mean a direct increase in the price per kilowatt-hour, CFE explainers note — instead, the range of consumption covered by the subsidy shrinks, so the same level of usage can produce a higher bill.

El Mañana puts numbers on the change for Nuevo Laredo's tariff 1E households: the summer subsidy covered up to 900 kilowatt-hours a month (1,800 bimonthly), while the winter period from November 1 through April subsidizes only 200 kilowatt-hours a month (400 bimonthly). Once usage passes 400 kilowatt-hours bimonthly, the article warns, the bill could nearly triple without the government support. CFE guidance cited by the paper recommends keeping heating at a steady 20 to 22 degrees Celsius — each extra degree adds 7 to 10 percent to consumption — and notes that a portable heater running five hours a day can alone use more than 200 kilowatt-hours a month.

That matters most for households that keep using air conditioning and other high-draw appliances at summer levels. Homes whose average consumption over the last 12 months exceeds the limit for their local tariff can also fall into the Doméstica de Alto Consumo (DAC) category, which carries no subsidy at all, according to CFE guidance.

The CFE's northern zone counts about 187,500 customers, covering Nuevo Laredo along with Camargo, Miguel Alemán, Mier and Guerrero in Tamaulipas, Lampazos and Anáhuac in Nuevo León, and Hidalgo and Candela in Coahuila, according to Noreste Digital. The subsidy ending in Nuevo Laredo is part of the same nationwide calendar that returns nine hot-climate states to regular tariffs on November 1, including Tamaulipas.

CFE advises customers to check their bills against their usage and to consult current domestic tariffs, consumption ranges and energy-saving tips on its portal at cfe.mx.

Sources:

  • El Mañana de Nuevo Laredo, "Desde hoy, la luz es más cara en Nuevo Laredo; termina subsidio," November 1, 2026
  • Noreste Digital, "A cuidar el gasto de luz; acaba subsidio y tendrá mayor costo," October 30, 2026

title: Nuevo Laredo power bills rise as summer electricity subsidy ends November 1
